conditions: There exists a folder named "Budget" in Box, uniquely identifiable by that name.
That folder has an owner — the Box user set in the folder's "owner" field (the owner collaborator role), not necessarily its creator.
Among all files, identify PDFs (file type/extension .pdf) whose modified_by is that owner.
Of those PDFs, select the one with the most recent modified_at timestamp — i.e., the PDF that owner most recently modified.
The tag "owner-edit" is added to that specific file.

readings: A folder whose name contains "Budget" as a recognizable label (e.g. "Budget 2025", "Budget Planning")

ambiguities.phrase: the owner of the Budget folder
readings: The user set as the folder's owner (Box's explicit owner field/role)
The user who originally created the folder

ambiguities.phrase: the PDF that the owner ... last modified
readings: Among PDF files, the one that owner most recently modified (filter to PDFs first, then take max timestamp)
The single most recently modified item by that owner overall, valid only if that item happens to be a PDF

records.note: Headcount plan.pdf: parent is Planning folder, but modified_by_id=30000000002 = Maya Chen, who is the Budget folder's owner (owned_by_id=30000000002). No other PDF has a later modification by her, so this is the correct target. Satisfies r1-r4; r5 is the action to perform, not a pre-existing condition.

Q4 summary.pdf sits inside the Budget folder itself (parent_id=3200), but its modified_by_id=30000000005 is Dana Whitfield, not Maya Chen (the folder's actual owner). This is a designed near-miss: a careless reader might pick it for being physically located in the Budget folder, but the request asks for the PDF modified by the folder's owner, not a PDF inside the folder. Under a careful reading it clearly fails r3 (wrong modifier) and consequently r4.

turn2.differences: The author's r1-r4 match my step-1 reading exactly. r5 (tag added) is really the action to execute rather than a filter condition distinguishing candidates, so it doesn't meaningfully 'fail' for either file - it's satisfied by definition once the correct file (3301) is acted on.

ambiguity_effects.explain: Only one folder is named exactly 'Budget' (id 3200); no other folder name contains 'Budget', so both candidate readings of the phrase converge on the same folder.

ambiguity_effects.phrase: the owner of the Budget folder
ambiguity_effects.explain: The Budget folder's owned_by_id (Maya Chen, 30000000002) differs from its created_by_id (Leo Park, 30000000004). Reading it as the explicit Box 'owner' field (Maya Chen) yields a match (3301). Reading it as 'whoever created the folder' (Leo Park) yields no match at all, since no PDF has modified_by_id=30000000004. A careful reader familiar with Box's data model would use the owner field, so this resolves cleanly rather than being a live ambiguity, but a careless reader could genuinely break the task by conflating owner with creator.

Both files in the dataset are PDFs, so there is no competing non-PDF file that would make the 'PDF-first filter' vs 'last item overall, happens to be PDF' readings diverge here. The ambiguity is moot given this data.

turn2.naturalness_note: The phrasing is a bit formal/convoluted for casual speech ('the PDF that the owner of the Budget folder last modified'), but it's a plausible way for someone coordinating shared folders to refer to a file without knowing its exact name. The tag name 'owner-edit' feels slightly synthetic (typical of a workflow/labeling convention) but not implausible as a real tagging scheme.
